messages:
Asha: hey all, new hire here. trying to use VSCode devcontainer for the web repo so my setup is reproducible. hitting three issues: 1) asdf versions inside the container vs host (shims mismatch), 2) git commits inside container are unsigned (we use GPG on host), and 3) I want 1Password secrets available in the container without committing .env. any recommended patterns?
Liam: welcome! :wave: short answers: install asdf inside the devcontainer image (so versions are deterministic), forward your GPG agent into the container for signing, and use direnv/op or a bind-mounted op session to provide secrets.
Nora: adding details: for ASDF, bake the language plugins and desired versions into the Dockerfile (or devcontainer Dockerfile) so `asdf install` runs at build time. avoids host/guest mismatch. if you need fast iteration, mounting $HOME/.asdf into the container works but can be messy.
Asha: I was mounting my host ~/.asdf and it felt flaky (host node showed up sometimes). will try baking into image. how to forward GPG?
Liam: two options we use: 1) mount the host gpg-agent socket into the container: `-v $HOME/.gnupg/S.gpg-agent:/home/dev/.gnupg/S.gpg-agent` and set `GPG_AGENT_INFO` or `GPG_SOCK` env. or 2) use SSH-agent style forwarding with `gpg-connect-agent` + socat. mounting the socket is simplest but check permissions.
Nora: note: with WSL or mac you may need to expose the socket path differently. also set `git config --global gpg.program /usr/bin/gpg` inside the container and ensure gnupg is installed there. then commits from the container are picked up by the host agent.
Asha: any security concerns with mounting the socket?
Liam: mount gives the container access to your private key via the agent, so only do it for trusted local dev images. avoid mounting to untrusted CI. use ephemeral containers or remove mount when done.
Nora: for 1Password: don't bake secrets. we prefer direnv + op inside the container or mounting a minimal session token. devcontainer.json can include a postCreateCommand that runs `eval $(op signin --raw)` interactively if you open the container from a WSL/host shell. alternatively, mount a file with the OP_SESSION token into the container at runtime (with strict file perms) and read it in entrypoint.
DevEnvBot: Pro tip: dev onboarding doc https://intranet/redwood/onboarding/devcontainer has recipes: Dockerfile+asdf example, gpg socket mount snippet, and a sample .devcontainer/devcontainer.json showing a safe op session helper.
Asha: great, last thing: direnv inside container or host?
Liam: run direnv inside container and keep .envrc in repo (gitignored secrets). direnv will source op read on `direnv allow` and works for processes launched inside the container.
OnboardingBot: Welcome Asha! If you want, we can pair on a devcontainer build tomorrow. See internal checklist at https://intranet/redwood/onboarding/devcontainer-setup.
Asha: thanks everyone, that gives me a clear plan. I'll bake asdf into the image and try the socket mount for gpg in a trusted local container, then switch to direnv+op for secrets. will ping if stuck. :thumbsup:
